testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When using controlled braking in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half your normal force.
Press the brakes until the wheels lock.
Press the brakes with very light pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep the steering wheel steady while braking this way.

questions.question: What happens if you use parking brakes in wet weather when it is below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release on their own.
The brakes may become too smooth to work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in wet weather when it is below freezing. The brakes could freeze and lock in place, making it impossible to move the vehicle.

questions.question: What may be in the air entering air storage tanks?
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the brake system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If it leaks faster, do not drive it—something needs repair.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain the tanks in an air brake system?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: You must drain the air storage tanks to remove water and compressor oil. If you do not, water can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What are air brakes?

options.text: An effective way to stop large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: An effective way to stop large vehicles.
questions.explanation: When properly maintained, air brakes are safe and effective for stopping large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, what happens?

options.text: The ABS will still help with steering control.
The ABS makes jackknifing more likely.
The ABS lets others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS will still help with steering control.
questions.explanation: If the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the ABS will still improve steering control. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: When do you need a tank endorsement?

options.text: When transporting both liquids and gases.
It is optional when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: When transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to drive a tank vehicle for transporting liquids or gases. This applies to both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: What should you do if the air pressure warning light comes on?

options.text: Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.
Safely leave the roadway and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely leave the roadway and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on, stop immediately and park safely. This warning means there is a problem with the air brake system that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in wet weather below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release on their own.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Using parking brakes in wet, freezing weather can cause the brakes to freeze and lock, preventing the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to warn that the system is not working properly.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS fails, your regular brakes will still work.

questions.question: The application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes in an air brake system. Not all air brake vehicles have this gauge.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, what happens if one system loses pressure?

options.text: The other system will supply air to fix the low system.
The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
The low system will use a backup system to refill the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front or rear brakes may not work properly.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. You must stop safely and get the air system repaired.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.
Only brakes on one side of the vehicle work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. Each system has its own air tanks and is connected to a single set of brake controls.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: To get normal stopping power, drivers with a front brake limiting valve should:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Studies show this is not helpful, so always leave it on "normal."

questions.question: Do not use the parking brake when parking if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.
There is water on the ground.

questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake if brakes are very hot from going down a steep hill, or if brakes are wet and it is freezing. Hot brakes can be damaged. Wet brakes in freezing weather can freeze up and make the vehicle stuck.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, you must wait for the air compressor to build at least ____ in both systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. This buildup can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If air tanks have manual drains, how often should you drain them?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day of driving. This prevents water and oil from building up in the system.

questions.question: What should you do with your service brakes?

options.text: Have a mechanic test them only.

questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before you drive. This helps you find any problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air tanks.

questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at once can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:

options.text: Be careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What must every air tank have in an air-braked vehicle?
questions.explanation: All air tanks must have a one-way check valve between the air compressor and the first tank. This valve stops air from leaking out.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles must have a low air pressure warning light. It is usually red and may have a buzzer.
